mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship between Team A's shots FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior) and goals FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior), cross-referenced with shots_on_target FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior). The mechanism asks whether a large positive divergence in shots is accompanied by a proportional divergence in goals and shots_on_target, or whether the shot surge is decoupled from on-target and scoring output.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots FOR rises sharply in recent matches relative to the long-run mean, goals FOR and shots_on_target FOR are expected to rise proportionally; if shots rise but shots_on_target and goals do not, the shot surge is suppressed in quality — a non-linear joint relationship between volume and quality observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly tracking Team A's shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into goals or represent a low-conversion regime.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly comparing two distinct observables (shots and goals, with shots_on_target as a third) across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it tests the joint co-movement (or divergence) of multiple observables across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5) is below its all-prior mean AND Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5) is above its all-prior mean, while simultaneously Team A is playing at home (where its shots_on_target FOR is higher than away). The mechanism tests whether this asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable configuration is associated with a widened shots_on_target differential.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR declines and shots_on_target AGAINST rises simultaneously, and Team A holds a home shots_on_target advantage, the combined shots_on_target differential in Team A's favour is expected to be wider than either team's individual observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a divergence between its shots_on_target FOR (declining in recent matches) and shots_on_target AGAINST (rising in recent matches), while its goals FOR has also declined recently. Jointly, this asymmetric cross-observable pattern — Team B generating fewer quality chances while conceding more — may interact with Team A's home shot advantage to produce a structurally skewed shot-on-target differential.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric joint relationship across different observables for the two sides (Team A's home shots_on_target FOR vs Team B's recent shots_on_target FOR and AGAINST), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single team's observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's possession FOR being structurally below 50% (both all-prior and recent-5), while simultaneously measuring whether Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR meet or exceed competition-context norms. The mechanism tests the joint relationship: does low possession suppress corner and shot production, or are they decoupled?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: For teams with chronic possession deficits, corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR are expected to be suppressed relative to competition norms; if they are not suppressed (or are elevated), this represents a decoupling — a non-linear joint relationship where possession level does not predict attacking volume observables in the usual direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates in a low-possession regime (chronically below 50%) but generates corners and shots at or above competition-context norms. This joint pattern — low possession combined with above-average attacking set-piece and shot production — tests whether possession deficit is decoupled from corner and shot output for this team, representing a non-standard joint relationship between a control observable and volume observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly comparing two distinct observables (possession and corners/shots) against a competition baseline simultaneously. It is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one band; it tests whether the joint state of two observables diverges from the expected co-movement.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state: Team A's goals AGAINST in the second half exceeds goals AGAINST in the first half (all-prior), AND Team B's goals FOR in the second half is at or above goals FOR in the first half (all-prior). The mechanism tests whether this aligned half-level asymmetry across both teams predicts a second-half-skewed goal distribution.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A concedes more in the second half and Team B scores more in the second half, the second half is expected to be more goal-productive than the first half for this fixture, representing a within-match state dependence that rises with the second-half period.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals conceded split between first and second halves reveals a back-loaded defensive vulnerability (more goals conceded in the second half than the first), while Team B's goals scored split shows a similar back-loading (more goals scored in the second half). The joint within-match state — both teams' half-level goal patterns aligning in the same direction — tests whether the second half is structurally more goal-productive for this fixture configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a half-level split (within-match state) jointly across both teams' goal observables (Team A AGAINST and Team B FOR), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band. It combines two distinct team-role perspectives at half resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state: Team A's fouls FOR exceeds fouls AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5), Team A's possession FOR is structurally below 50%, and Team B's possession is near-neutral. The mechanism tests whether the combination of high foul-committing and low possession (a two-dimensional conditioning) is associated with elevated second-half card accumulation, beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team commits more fouls than it receives AND operates in a low-possession regime, its second-half card rate is expected to rise relative to competition norms, with the joint condition producing a stronger association than either foul rate or possession deficit alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Cards in the second half (cards_2h) can be jointly examined against the fouls FOR and possession patterns of both teams. Team A commits more fouls than it receives (higher fouls FOR than fouls AGAINST), while Team B also commits fouls at a moderate rate. The joint relationship between a team's foul-committing tendency and its second-half card accumulation — conditioned on the possession imbalance (Team A low possession, Team B near-neutral) — tests whether foul volume under possession deficit predicts elevated second-half card rates.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (foul-committing tendency AND possession level) to condition the second-half card outcome. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band; it tests a two-dimensional joint conditioning on cards_2h.
